title: EventIdentity
description: Canonical structured output for the event creative brief (event_identity_schema_v6, spec.md §7.5). A creative brief only: it carries no operational event fact. Runtime may narrow the typography-category enum to enabled catalog values.

hostConcept.description: Decided first, from the host's own words: 'open' when the host left the look to us (nothing beyond the occasion, 'surprise me'); 'cues' when they gave a creative cue (a palette, a mood, a motif, a person's interests, a place's character) but no concept or style of their own; 'own' when they named a clear concept or style of their own (a named format such as an album cover, poster, magazine or storybook page; an explicit list of motifs; a decade or era; a named aesthetic; or how the artwork should look). The theme seed is used only when 'open'; code suggests no rendering when 'own'.

creativeDirection.description: Concise 1-3 sentence creative thesis for the event's visual world. No card implementation choices (layouts, fonts, colours as hex, positions).

toneKeywords.description: Ranked/curated tone adjectives or short phrases with minimal synonym redundancy.

colorsExplicitlyConstrained.description: True only when the host explicitly narrows/requires/excludes palette families.

requiredColors.description: Hard color requirements in short natural language; preserve exact user hex strings when provided.

dominanceNotes.description: How palette families should dominate/recede; empty string when unspecified.

toneExplicitlyConstrained.description: True only when the host explicitly constrains light/mid/dark tonal space.

compatibleTypographyCategories.description: Ranked best-first compatible broad typography categories (not fonts). The card design picks a curated pairing from these categories. Do not pad with incompatible values.

visualMotifs.description: Subjects, objects, botanicals, scenery and patterns in natural language that could anchor or support the card's artwork (e.g. 'heirloom teddy in a tartan bow', 'lemon branches with blossom', 'fine double-rule border'). A close homage to a brand's character may be described in plain visual words; never IDs, logos, wordmarks, or brand, character or real people's names (spec.md §7.6). Every motif the host explicitly lists is kept; one left out for a product rule is named in designConstraints.

textureDirection.description: Visual and tactile character of the artwork, carrying any signal the host gave about how it should look, e.g. 'crisp photographic realism with natural light', 'glossy soft-lit 3D', 'flat matte graphic fields', 'fine engraved line with subtle grain', 'soft gouache on cream laid paper'. Never default to painted or watercolour.

typographyDirection.description: Typographic character/hierarchy, not a raw font-family choice.

copyTone.description: The voice of the card's wording and guest-facing copy, e.g. 'warm, concise, polished, not precious'.

designConstraints.description: Host-specific aesthetic constraints, including important negative constraints.

inspirationSummary.description: Compact summary of inspiration evidence; exactly 'No visual inspiration supplied.' when none exists.

$comment: event_identity_schema_v6 (owner decisions, 2026-10-06): adds the required hostConcept, decided first, so code gives the design a random rendering suggestion only when the host named no concept or style of their own, and the identity uses the theme seed only when the host left the look to us; the visualMotifs description keeps every motif the host lists and names no real person. v5 (Phase 5): the textureDirection description no longer leads with gouache and carries the host's rendering signal; structure unchanged. v4 (Revision 7.1): visualMotifs allows a plain-words homage to a brand's character, never logos, wordmarks or names. v3 (Revision 7): removed compatibleTonalDirections and compatibleFamilies; visualMotifs names subjects that can anchor the card's artwork.
